page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by 32 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 256 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The hardware configuration includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and uses the arm64 architecture, which lacks x86-specific vector extensions like AVX but includes native cryptographic acceleration.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8gd.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier memory performance, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 405.8 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 184.15 GB/sec. Its database capabilities are highlighted by a top-tier Passmark database operations score and strong Redis SET performance of 68.24 million operations per second. Multi-core processing is highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21506.0. However, the instance shows limitations in LLM text generation, where it scores in the bottom 25% for small model text generation and large model prompt processing.

The custom Graviton ARMv9 architecture and integrated NVMe storage deliver high qualitative cost efficiency by reducing power consumption and eliminating the need for external block storage for high-I/O operations. This resource density makes the instance highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, real-time analytics, and software compilation. It is less suitable for workloads requiring dedicated GPU acceleration or x86-specific instruction sets.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized, arm64-based server instance powered by 32 dedicated AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 256 GB of RAM, 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show top-tier memory bandwidth, with large-block reads at 405.8 GB/sec, and exceptional database performance, including a top-tier Passmark database score and 68.24 million Redis SET operations per second. While multi-core CPU performance is strong, the instance exhibits weaker performance in LLM text generation tasks. Qualitatively, the custom ARM architecture and bundled high-speed local storage offer excellent cost efficiency for memory-bound and high-I/O workloads. It is highly recommended for relational databases, in-memory caching, and data-intensive applications.
